blockMcqs.question: Which SQL sublanguage controls who can access database objects?
options: TCL — COMMIT and ROLLBACK
DML — INSERT and UPDATE
DCL — GRANT and REVOKE
DDL — CREATE and ALTER
blockMcqs.explanation: DCL (Data Control Language) consists of GRANT and REVOKE, which manage access permissions on database objects.

blockMcqs.question: What is the main network benefit of stored procedures?
options: They cache query results automatically
They compress data before sending
One CALL replaces many round-trips
They encrypt the connection
blockMcqs.explanation: The app sends a single CALL; all the SQL executes inside the server, reducing network round-trips.

blockMcqs.question: A function differs from a procedure in that it must:
options: Use only DDL statements
Return exactly one scalar value
Accept no parameters
Always commit its changes
blockMcqs.explanation: A function returns a single scalar value and can be used inside SQL expressions; a procedure uses OUT parameters instead.

blockMcqs.question: A BEFORE INSERT trigger fires:
options: After the new row is committed
Before the row change reaches the table
Once per transaction, not per row
Only when a COMMIT is issued
blockMcqs.explanation: A BEFORE trigger runs before the DML change is written, letting you validate or modify the data first.

blockMcqs.question: Why are cursors slower than set-based SQL on large tables?
options: They cannot use indexes
They require a separate database connection
They process one row at a time instead of the full set
They disable transaction logging
blockMcqs.explanation: Cursors loop row by row, bypassing the optimizer's ability to process the whole result set in one engine operation.

blockMcqs.question: What does granting a privilege to a role achieve?
options: It copies the privilege into each user's profile permanently
It encrypts the objects the role can access
All members of that role inherit the privilege
It removes the same privilege from other roles
blockMcqs.explanation: Roles bundle privileges; all users assigned the role automatically receive those privileges.

blockMcqs.question: What does ROLLBACK TO a savepoint do?
options: Commits all changes up to that savepoint
Undoes the entire transaction from the start
Undoes changes back to that savepoint, keeping earlier work
Deletes the savepoint and all data since it
blockMcqs.explanation: ROLLBACK TO only undoes work done after the savepoint; changes before it are preserved and can still be committed.

blockMcqs.question: Which risk is most associated with trigger chains?
options: They prevent any COMMIT from succeeding
Hidden cascading logic that is hard to trace and debug
They automatically grant extra privileges
They disable index usage on affected tables
blockMcqs.explanation: Chained triggers create hidden side effects — one INSERT can cascade into many downstream operations that are invisible to the original caller.
